title: Deep anomaly and boosting models predict seven cancers from national health checkup data
summary: Korean National Insurance System checkup data (adults 40 and over, checked every 2 years) were analyzed with logistic regression, LightGBM, neural networks, survival analysis and a one-class embedding classifier based on deep learning anomaly detection. The one-class embedding classifier had the highest AUC for each cancer: 0.868 liver, 0.849 lung, 0.798 colorectal, 0.746 pancreatic, 0.800 gastric, 0.749 breast and 0.790 cervical; models were externally validated on a tertiary hospital checkup database. The study is retrospective, several AUCs are moderate, and the abstract excerpt does not state which cohort each AUC refers to.
